statements.consumer: Analysts tuning conditional causal bounds can distinguish whether covariate smoothness, rather than outcome smoothness, blocks regular inference.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(F_{a,z}(y)=\int_0^yq_{a,n}(v,z)dv\), \(Q_{a,z}=F_{a,z}^{-1}\), and
\[
H_z(y)=F_{1,z}(y)-F_{0,z}(y)=\int_0^y\Delta_n(v,z)dv.
\]
If \(u_z=\mathcal G_{n,z}\Delta_n(\cdot,z)\), integrating its Neumann equation gives
\[
-\bar q_n(y,z)\partial_yu_z(y)=H_z(y).
\]
Because \(H_z(0)=H_z(1)=0\), integration by parts yields
\[
\int_0^1\Delta_n(y,z)u_z(y)dy
=\int_0^1\bar q_n(y,z)\{\partial_yu_z(y)\}^2dy
=\int_0^1\frac{H_z(y)^2}{\bar q_n(y,z)}dy.                                \tag{1}
\]
For each \(u\in(0,1)\), the mean-value identity and \(c\le q_{a,n}\le C\) give
\[
H_z\{Q_{0,z}(u)\}
=q_{1,n}(\zeta_{u,z},z)\{Q_{0,z}(u)-Q_{1,z}(u)\}
\]
for some \(\zeta_{u,z}\) between the two quantiles.  Changing variables \(u=F_{0,z}(y)\) and applying the same bounds gives
\[
c_3\int_0^1H_z(y)^2dy
\le W_2^2(Q_{0,n}(\cdot\mid z),Q_{1,n}(\cdot\mid z))
\le C_3\int_0^1H_z(y)^2dy.                                                \tag{2}
\]
Combining (1)--(2), integrating against \(R_n\), and using \(\rho_n\le\rho\), we obtain
\[
c_4\rho_n^2\le\theta_n\le C_4\rho_n^2\le C_4\rho^2.                    \tag{3}
\]
Thus the zero estimator has root-mean-square risk at most \(C_4\rho^2\).

For the observable upper bound, put
\[
p_n=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3
+\rho^{\,2/(2+3/s_y+d/s_z)}\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^2.
\]
The Hoeffding identity underlying the expansion theorem, before imposing a little-oh condition, is
\[
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y,J_z,n}-\theta_n
=\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}+\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}
+B^y_{J_y,n}+B^z_{J_z,n}+R_{J_y,J_z,n}.                                  \tag{4}
\]
We require an \(L^2\) bound on its final term.  The number of pilot coefficients is
\[
\overline D_n\asymp2^{\bar J_y+d\bar J_z}
\asymp(n/\log n)^{1/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
The coefficientwise exponential-moment calculation from the pilot-control proof, summed over \(O(\overline D_n)\) coefficients, gives for fixed \(x\in[0,1]\)
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}
P\!\left(\max_e\left[\|\widehat r_n^{(-e)}-r_n\|_\infty
+\max_a\|\widehat q_{a,n}^{(-e)}-q_{a,n}\|_\infty\right]
>C\{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}+x\}\right)
\le C\exp\{-cnx^2/\overline D_n\}.                                      \tag{5}
\]
The projection bias is \(O(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n})\); ratios and normalization are Lipschitz on the positivity event, and clipping keeps the pilots bounded off that event.  Integrating the tail in (5) proves the corresponding fixed-moment bounds.  The deterministic Taylor and interpolation inequalities proved in the pilot-control lemma therefore imply
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}\|R_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_{L^2(P)}
\le Cp_n+o\!\left(\frac\rho{\sqrt n}+\frac{A_{J_y,J_z,n}}n
+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}+2^{-2s_zJ_z}\right).                                   \tag{6}
\]
Orthogonality of the two Hoeffding projections, their variance formulas, and \(\rho_n\le\rho\) give
\[
\|\mathbb L_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_2\le C\rho n^{-1/2},
\qquad
\|\mathbb U_{J_y,J_z,n}\|_2\le C A_{J_y,J_z,n}/n.                       \tag{7}
\]
At \((J_y^*,J_z^*)\), the spectrum, bias, and tuning results give
\[
A_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}/n\asymp r_{n,d}(s_z),
\qquad
|B^y_{J_y^*,n}|+|B^z_{J_z^*,n}|\le Cr_{n,d}(s_z).                         \tag{8}
\]
Minkowski's inequality applied to (4), followed by (6)--(8), proves
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}
\{E_P(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{an}}_{J_y^*,J_z^*,n}-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\le C\{\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)+p_n\}.                                \tag{9}
\]
For the known class radius \(\rho\), select the zero map or this explicit sample map according to which displayed guarantee is smaller.  Equations (3) and (9) prove the asserted upper bound; in particular the zero map is selected when \(\rho\lesssim\rho_{Q,n}\).

For the converse, use the explicit sign-paired family.  Choose its fixed \(c_0\) small enough that
\[
\chi^2(\overline{\mathbb P}_n,\mathbb P_n^0)\le\eta<1.
\]
The inequality \(\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\{\chi^2(P,Q)\}^{1/2}/2\), obtained by Cauchy--Schwarz from the likelihood ratio, makes the total variation strictly smaller than one.  The null endpoint is zero, while every mixture component has endpoint at least
\[
\delta_n=c_5\min\{\rho^2,r_{n,d}(s_z)\}.
\]
For any estimator, thresholding at \(\delta_n/2\) produces a test, and on either testing error the squared estimation error is at least \(\delta_n^2/4\).  Since the sum of the two testing errors is at least one minus total variation, this proves
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,d}}
\{E_P(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\ge c_6\min\{\rho^2,r_{n,d}(s_z)\}.                                      \tag{10}
\]

For the regular direction, extend \(q_{a,t}^0\) constantly in \(z\).  When \(\rho\ge Kn^{-1/2}\), compare \(t=c_7\rho\) and \(t'=t+c_8n^{-1/2}\), choosing fixed constants small enough that both inverse-elliptic radii are at most \(\rho\).  The Hellinger calculation in the mixture-check lemma leaves their testing affinity bounded away from zero.  Let \(\Theta(t)\) be the endpoint on this symmetric cosine path.  Here
\[
F_{a,t}(y)=y+(2a-1)t\sin(2\pi y)/(4\pi),
\qquad \partial_yF_{a,t}=q_{a,t}^0\ge c.
\]
Implicit differentiation gives
\[
\partial_tQ_{a,t}(u)
=-\frac{(2a-1)\sin\{2\pi Q_{a,t}(u)\}}
{4\pi q_{a,t}^0\{Q_{a,t}(u)\}}.
\]
Differentiating this bounded quotient once more shows that \(\Theta''\) is continuous near zero.  The cosine lemma gives \(\Theta'(0)=0\) and \(\Theta''(0)=1/(4\pi^2)\); hence, on a fixed small neighborhood, \(\Theta''(v)\ge1/(8\pi^2)\).  Integrating twice gives
\[
|\Theta(t')-\Theta(t)|\ge c_9t|t'-t|\ge c_{10}\rho n^{-1/2}.              \tag{11}
\]
The same two-point testing reduction yields a lower bound \(c_{11}\rho n^{-1/2}\).  If \(\rho<Kn^{-1/2}\), then \(r_{n,d}(s_z)\ge n^{-1}\gtrsim\rho^2\), because \(4s_z/(4s_z+d)<1\), so (10) already gives order \(\rho^2\).  Splitting on these two cases proves
\[
\max\!\left[\min\{\rho^2,r_{n,d}(s_z)\},
\rho n^{-1/2}\mathbf1\{\rho\ge Kn^{-1/2}\}\right]
\asymp\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\},                         \tag{12}
\]
and hence the lower frontier.

If \(p_n=O\{\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\}\), (9)--(12) match.  Otherwise (9) and (10)--(12) are exactly the stated honest bracket.  Finally,
\[
\rho_{Q,n}^2=r_{n,d}(s_z)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\rho_{Q,n}=n^{-2s_z/(4s_z+d)},
\]
and
\[
\rho_{L,n}n^{-1/2}=r_{n,d}(s_z)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\rho_{L,n}=n^{(d-4s_z)/\{2(4s_z+d)\}}.
\]
Thus \(\rho_{L,n}\to0\) exactly when \(s_z>d/4\), which yields the displayed zero, quadratic, mixed, and regular zones.  If \(s_z\le d/4\), then \(r_{n,d}(s_z)\gtrsim n^{-1/2}\), while the first projection is identically zero at equality and (10) retains quadratic difficulty of at least root-\(n\) order.  A uniformly positive-variance regular root-\(n\) limit is therefore impossible over the class.

statements.statement:
Assume \(L>1\). When \(d=0\), use the no-covariate growing-outcome-resolution construction rather than setting \(d=0\) in the conditional tuning rule. Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)\),
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}\{E(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}\asymp\mathfrak R_{n,0}(s_y,s_z,\rho)=\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}.
\]
At equality under the uniform density, the full-sample bias-retaining estimator has the exact benchmark
\[
n\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}\Rightarrow2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{2}{\pi^2k^2}\xi_{1,k}^2,
\]
where \(J_y^0\to\infty\), \(2^{J_y^0}=o(n)\), and \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}=o(n^{-1})\). Subtracting \(2\sum_{k\le2^{J_y^0}}(\pi^2k^2)^{-1}/n\) yields the centered chaos. Thus the outcome resolution genuinely grows, the quadratic scale is \(n^{-1}\), and \(\rho_{Q,n}=\rho_{L,n}=n^{-1/2}\). This is the two-sample specialization of the del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet weighted quantile-process law.
statements.justification: A separate full-sample estimator is necessary to recover the classical two-sample constant rather than a split-sample direct-sum surrogate.
statements.gap: delBarrioGineUtzet2005 gives the unconditional quantile-process limit but not its role as the \(d=0\) branch of a conditional smoothness--degeneracy frontier.
statements.consumer: The result is the required sanity check and supplies exact simulation critical values when no covariate adjustment is used.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(d=0\), retain the notation \(F_a,Q_a\), and \(H=F_1-F_0\) from the frontier proof.  Its equations (1)--(3) use only the one-dimensional conditional-density bounds, so
\[
\theta_n=\|Q_1-Q_0\|_{L^2(0,1)}^2\asymp\rho_n^2\le\rho^2.                 \tag{1}
\]
Let \(D=Q_1-Q_0\), \(\widehat D=\widehat Q_{1,n}-\widehat Q_{0,n}\), and \(P_J=P^Q_J\).  Orthogonality gives the exact identity
\[
\widehat\theta^0_{J,n}-\theta_n
=2\langle P_JD,P_J(\widehat D-D)\rangle
+\|P_J(\widehat D-D)\|_2^2-\|(I-P_J)D\|_2^2.                             \tag{2}
\]

Represent an observation from arm \(a\) as \(Q_a(U_i)\), where the \(U_i\) are independent uniforms.  On \((k-1)/n<u\le k/n\), \(\widehat Q_{a,n}(u)=Q_a(U_{(k)})\).  Positivity makes \(Q_a\) \(c^{-1}\)-Lipschitz.  Direct integration of the beta density of \(U_{(k)}\) gives mean \(k/(n+1)\), variance \(k(n+1-k)/\{(n+1)^2(n+2)\}\), and fourth centered moment at most \(C/n^2\).  Because \(|k/(n+1)-u|\le2/n\), integration over all quantile cells yields
\[
E\|\widehat Q_{a,n}-Q_a\|_2^2\le Cn^{-1},
\qquad
E\|\widehat Q_{a,n}-Q_a\|_2^4\le Cn^{-2}.                                \tag{3}
\]
For the second inequality, use \((\int e^2)^2\le\int e^4\) on the unit interval.  Independence and the triangle inequality give the same orders for \(\widehat D-D\).

The density smoothness and positivity imply \(Q_a'=1/(q_{a,n}\circ Q_a)\).  Iterating the defining H\"older difference bound through composition and reciprocal operations shows that \(Q_a\in\mathcal C^{s_y+1}\) with a uniform norm bound.  Wavelet regularity and vanishing moments then give
\[
\|(I-P_J)D\|_2^2\le C2^{-2(s_y+1)J}.                                     \tag{4}
\]
Applying Cauchy--Schwarz and Minkowski's inequality to (2), followed by (1), (3), and (4), yields
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,0}}
\{E_P(\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\le C\{\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}+2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y^0}\}
\le C'\{\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}.                                        \tag{5}
\]
The zero estimator has risk at most \(C\rho^2\) by (1).  Selecting the better explicit map proves the upper bound \(C\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}\).

For the lower bound, compare \(t=0\) with \(t=c_0\min\{\rho,n^{-1/2}\}\) in the fixed-frequency family.  The mixture-check Hellinger calculation is bounded, and the cosine second variation gives endpoint separation
\[
c\min\{\rho^2,n^{-1}\}.                                                  \tag{6}
\]
For \(\rho\ge Kn^{-1/2}\), instead compare \(t=c_1\rho\) with \(t'=t+c_2n^{-1/2}\).  Small fixed constants keep both laws inside the radius-\(\rho\) class and their testing affinity bounded away from zero.  The twice-integrated cosine-path argument used in (11) of the frontier proof gives separation at least \(c_3\rho n^{-1/2}\).  Thresholding any estimator into a test, as in (10) of that proof, combines these separations into
\[
\inf_{\widetilde\theta_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{n,0}}
\{E_P(\widetilde\theta_n-\theta_n)^2\}^{1/2}
\ge c\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\}.                               \tag{7}
\]
Together with (5), this proves the minimax assertion.

At the uniform null, apply the revalidated quantile-process lemma independently to the two arms.  The omitted lower-tail squared norm is bounded by \((U_{(1)}+n^{-1})^2\), and the upper-tail term by the analogous expression involving \(1-U_{(n)}\).  The beta moments used in (3) make both \(o_P(1)\).  Hence the full quantile processes have the same \(L^2\) limits as their truncated versions.  Independence and symmetry of the bridge imply
\[
Z_n:=\sqrt n(\widehat Q_{1,n}-\widehat Q_{0,n})
\Rightarrow\mathbb B_1-\mathbb B_0\stackrel d=\sqrt2\,\mathbb B
\quad\text{in }L^2(0,1).                                                  \tag{8}
\]
The projectors \(P^Q_{J_y^0}\) are contractions and converge strongly to the identity because \(J_y^0\to\infty\).  Strong convergence is uniform on compact subsets of \(L^2\), and tightness from (8) therefore gives \(\|(I-P^Q_{J_y^0})Z_n\|_2=o_P(1)\).  Continuity of the squared \(L^2\)-norm now yields
\[
n\widehat\theta^0_{J_y^0,n}
=\|P^Q_{J_y^0}Z_n\|_2^2
\Rightarrow2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt.                                   \tag{9}
\]

The bridge covariance kernel is \(K(s,t)=s\wedge t-st\).  Differentiating its integral operator twice, with zero boundary values, shows that \(\sqrt2\sin(\pi kt)\) are orthonormal eigenfunctions with eigenvalues \((\pi^2k^2)^{-1}\).  Gaussian orthogonality makes their coordinates independent standard normals, so Parseval's identity gives
\[
2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt
\stackrel d=\sum_{k=1}^\infty\frac{2}{\pi^2k^2}\xi_{1,k}^2.               \tag{10}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
2\sum_{k\le2^{J_y^0}}\frac1{\pi^2k^2}\longrightarrow
2\sum_{k=1}^\infty\frac1{\pi^2k^2}=\frac13
=E\left\{2\int_0^1\mathbb B(t)^2dt\right\}.
\]
Subtracting the corresponding finite sum divided by \(n\) from the estimator therefore centers the limit in (9)--(10).  Finally, both \(\rho^2=n^{-1}\) and \(\rho n^{-1/2}=n^{-1}\) give \(\rho=n^{-1/2}\), proving \(\rho_{Q,n}=\rho_{L,n}=n^{-1/2}\).

statements.statement: Can the mixed linear--quadratic calibration handle construct \(\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\) such that \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{0\le\rho\le1}\inf_{(P_{0,n},P_{1,n})\in\mathcal M_{n,d}(s_y,s_z,\rho)}P\{\theta_n\in\mathcal I_n^{\mathrm{mix}}\}\ge1-\alpha,\] with expected half-width of order \(\rho n^{-1/2}+r_{n,d}(s_z)\) for pilot-feasible \(d\ge1\), order \(\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}\) for \(d=0\), and the regular Gaussian width implied by SmoothCOT Theorem 3.2 at each fixed unequal law? The construction must derive uniform spectral-tail, anti-concentration, multiplier-coupling, observable pilot-Hessian, covariance, and anisotropic bias-envelope control from the primitive model class.
statements.justification: Uniform calibration is the genuine unresolved step needed to report one interval without pretesting equality.
statements.gap: ChenFang2019 treats fixed second-order maps, SturmaDrtonLeung2024 Gaussianizes incomplete U-statistics, and AgarwalLuedtke2026 retains fixed entropic damping; none controls a growing unregularized anisotropic Hessian and two bias tails together.
statements.consumer: A positive answer gives one defensible uncertainty report for the \(\mathsf{STAR}\) conditional bound across equality and fixed alternatives.

statements.statement: Let \(U_1,\ldots,U_n\) be independent uniform random variables on \((0,1)\), let \(G_n^{-1}\) be their empirical quantile function, set \(u_n(t)=\sqrt n\{t-G_n^{-1}(t)\}\), and define \(u_n^{\mathrm{tr}}(t)=u_n(t)\mathbf 1\{1/n<t<1-1/n\}\).  Then \(u_n^{\mathrm{tr}}\Rightarrow\mathbb B\) weakly in \(L^2(0,1)\), where \(\mathbb B\) is a standard Brownian bridge.

sampling_model.design: Two independent randomized treatment-arm samples, each of even size \(n=2m\), with deterministic equal folds of size \(m\).
sampling_model.units: Observations are \(W_{a,i,n}=(Y_{a,i,n},Z_{a,i,n})\), with scalar outcome support \([0,1]\) and covariate support \([0,1]^d\).
sampling_model.treatment: Randomized arm membership directly samples the two potential-outcome marginals.
sampling_model.overlap: Propensity overlap is not used; the arm laws share the marginal \(R_n\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For \(d\ge1\), opposite-fold joint and marginal wavelet projections are conditionally normalized and clipped to fixed positive bounds. Their averaged conditional density enters a zero-outcome-mean ridge Galerkin inverse, which defines the observed Hessian, first-order score, diagonal-free kernel, and foldwise variance estimator even off the clipping-inactive event. For \(d=0\), the separate branch uses the full empirical quantile processes.

tldr: For \(d\ge1\), conditional squared Wasserstein distance has an anisotropic boundary geometry: inverse ellipticity smooths outcome frequencies while covariate resolution replicates the ordered spectrum. A min--max comparison gives Hilbert--Schmidt norm \(\asymp2^{dJ_z/2}\), outcome bias \(2^{-2(s_y+1)J_y}\), and covariate bias \(2^{-2s_zJ_z}\). A fully observed two-fold statistic uses clipped-and-normalized opposite-fold density pilots, a ridge Galerkin inverse, explicit first-order scores, and a diagonal-free second-order kernel. In the pilot-feasible smoothness region, balancing the three scales yields local rate \(\min\{\rho^2,\rho n^{-1/2}+n^{-4s_z/(4s_z+d)}\}\) and elbow \(s_z=d/4\), matched by the sign-paired converse; the limit statement is an \(n\)-dependent Gaussian-quadratic approximation, with chaos only under \(\ell^2\) spectral convergence. The separate \(d=0\) branch recovers the two-sample del Barrio--Gin\'e--Utzet law and \(n^{-1}\) scale. Uniform mixed-regime calibration remains open.

project_justification.gap: SmoothCOT Section 3.3, Theorem 3.2, Remark 3.2, and Appendix C.4 stop at a regular CLT and faster-than-root-\(n\) equality statement. Existing unconditional Wasserstein laws, changing-kernel theory, fixed-entropic causal transport, and the direct-estimation COT abstract do not provide a verified observable equality-local anisotropic frontier.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a primitive smoothness-by-equality frontier that separates outcome elliptic smoothing from covariate rank and also recovers the unconditional \(d=0\) benchmark with the correct estimator and constants.
project_justification.fill: The project derives canonical ordered-spectrum and bias bounds, constructs the foldwise clipped ridge-Galerkin statistic, states the normalized triangular experiment and regular studentization with exact split constants, matches the pilot-feasible rate using a checked sign-paired wavelet family, and isolates honest all-regime calibration as the unresolved node.

related_work: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's SmoothCOT Section 3.3 gives quadratic stability, Theorem 3.2 gives the regular Gaussian law, Remark 3.2 records faster-than-root-\(n\) convergence at equality, and Appendix C.4 proves the CLT; the mixed triangular theorem strictly tightens that scalar randomized-arm specialization. Their AISTATS 2026 paper, verified only through its arXiv abstract and proceedings metadata, advertises a direct consistent nonparametric conditional-OT value estimator and a convergence rate. Formula-level overlap with the equality-local frontier remains externally unverifiable because its proceedings theorem text was inaccessible, so it is treated only as informing the project. Goldman, Huesmann, and Otto motivate inverse-elliptic linearization. Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart inform changing-kernel approximation. Del Barrio, Gin\'e, and Utzet provide the weighted quantile-process law recovered by the separate \(d=0\) branch. Chen and Fang motivate derivative-aware calibration, and Sturma, Drton, and Leung inform multiplier coupling. Agarwal and Luedtke analyze fixed-entropic causal transport. Niles-Weed and Berthet provide negative-order wavelet geometry; Manole and Niles-Weed provide unconditional separation-sensitive rates. Goldfeld, Kato, Nietert, and Rioux treat fixed Gaussian smoothing. Neykov, Wasserman, Kim, and Balakrishnan develop multiresolution conditional Wasserstein testing. Bickel and Ritov and Ingster and Suslina inform the explicit sign-mixture converse.
technical_internal_limitation: The cosine witness reduces one lower-bound channel to a covariate quadratic functional, but the observable upper expansion still requires uniform control of a density-dependent ridge Galerkin inverse. The optimal sup-norm pilot rate makes the advertised \(s_z\)-driven upper frontier available only when \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pil},n}^3=o(r_{n,d}(s_z))\). Full operator-norm covariance estimation additionally requires \(D_{J_y,J_z}\log n=o(m)\) and is used only for an observed spectral proxy, not for the point estimator.
honest_scope: The model has scalar compactly supported outcomes, equal randomized arm sizes, a shared covariate marginal, positive anisotropic H\"older densities, and known smoothness. The sharp conditional upper and lower frontier is stated for \(d\ge1\) only in the explicit pilot-feasible region; outside it the Rademacher lower bound remains, but no observable upper rate is claimed. The primary limit result is triangular, and a fixed Gaussian-chaos limit requires \(\ell^2\) convergence of normalized spectra and shifts. The \(d=0\) result uses a separate full-sample empirical-quantile branch. Adaptation, multivariate outcomes, observational propensity estimation, observed spectral plug-in at high dimension, and uniform mixed calibration are open.
